subject: Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
parts:
Hi all,

I'm attempting to set up a simple remote application using shinyapps.io, but have hit a bit of a snag. What I'm looking to do is create a very simple survey which can be remotely deployed, but uses the local shiny interface defined by the mirtCAT package wrapper function (install.packages('mirtCAT')). E.g., locally, this works fine:

```{r}
library(mirtCAT)
options <- matrix(c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"),
                  nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
df <- data.frame(Question = c('Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3'), Option = options, Type = "radio")

## Run the mirtCAT web interface and store results
results <- mirtCAT(df = df)
```

Using some variant of this, I created a single executable source file called 'app.R', and uploaded it to the shinyapps.io location (http://philchalmers.shinyapps.io/mirtCAT-shinyapp_io). The problem is that, because mirtCAT calls shiny::runApp() internally and does a lot of pre and post processing, everything really needs to be deployed using a single R script (not a separate server.R and ui.R file). 

After uploading the app.R file, I simply get the following: 'ERROR: Key / already in use', which likely is what is expected given my approach. Any tips or tricks to tell shinyapps to just source the app.R file and trust that runApp() is run internally would be greatly appreciated. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
parts:
Hi Phil, it looks like you're the author of this package?

I'd refactor the mirtCAT function to pull everything up to the runApp() into a separate function--let's call it createShinyApp. Then change the runApp() call to a shinyApp() call (so the createShinyApp function returns the result of shinyApp()).

Back in mirtCAT, you can call runApp(createShinyApp(...), launch.browser=TRUE) like you were before.

Your app.R on the other hand can call createShinyApp(...) as the last line in the file and that should work with shinyapps.io.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Application with a single script that implicitly calls shiny::runApp()
parts:
Hi Joe,

Thanks so much for the suggestion. I think I understand what you mean, but just to clarify. I should set up a script with something like this:

- In 'app.R':

  R> mirtCAT_preamble()
  R> createShinyApp()

That makes sense to me. However, normally there is post-processing which occurs after the app has been run (doing some general organization of the returned result, which I guess I could move into server.R, but also doing things like sending the results to a configured Dropbox folder). Must the createShinyApp() be on the final line? 

If so, that complicates things in that all of the post-processing must go into the server.R file, and, given that the rDrop package is not on CRAN, I can't really update mirtCAT to allow for this method in the next update (the whole point of using shinyapps.io was to make some insentitive surveys public). Perhaps there are better ways to get results off the shinyapp.io server effectively? Cheers.

Phil
